chunks: It was narrated to me by Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Sa'd ibn Abdillah from Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal from Ghalib ibn Uthman from Shu'aib from a man from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
One who controls himself when he desires, when he fears, when he lusts, and when he becomes angry, Allah will prohibit his body from the Fire.

key_terms.حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ جَسَدَهُ عَلَى النَّارِ: Allah prohibited his body from the Fire (i.e., spared him from Hell)

ai.seo_question: What are the four states in which controlling oneself leads to salvation from Hellfire according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A’mal*, this hadith highlights the eschatological reward of *malk al-nafs* (self-mastery) by linking emotional regulation during desire, fear, lust, and anger to the physical preservation of the body from Hellfire. In Shia scholarship, this reflects the concept of *jihad al-nafs* (struggle against the self), where controlling these four primary drivers of human action is seen as a prerequisite for spiritual purity and divine acceptance.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. It was narrated to me by Ahmad b. Muhammad from Sa’d b. Abdillah from Muhammad b. Isa from al-Hassan b. Ali b. Fadhal from Ghalib b. Uthman from Shu’aib from a man from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said: “
One who controls himself at the time of fear and anger, Allah will prohibit fire for his body.”
